title: Introduce auditable surface variants and proportional gutter system
creator: Alyssa Chen
description:
Problem: Our current token set has grown ad-hoc over multiple releases and creates visual drift across buttons, tables, and charts. Teams are implementing local overrides which complicates QA and increases visual regressions. We need a single, auditable surface token layer plus a proportional gutter/spacing system that scales with component density.

Scope:
- Define a limited set of semantic surface variants (surface-0..surface-5) with explicit contrast targets and intended use cases (backgrounds, cards, overlays, controls).
- Introduce proportional gutter tokens (gutter-xs..gutter-xl) that are derived from a base spacing token and scale with density breakpoints.
- Re baseline typography ramp for compact and regular densities (type-compact scale + type-regular scale).
- Standardize elevation shadow stacks with three perceptual intensity presets (shadow-soft, shadow-medium, shadow-strong) and map them to surface variants.
- Provide a migration plan and codemod guidance for components: buttons, table rows/cells, chart panels, and modal surfaces.

Goals:
- Reduce token surface variance by 60% across core components.
- Meet WCAG AA contrast for text on all surface variants or provide explicit exceptions with guidance.
- Make spacing predictable for embedded widgets and tables using proportional gutters.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We choose semantic surface tokens over direct color tokens to decouple usage from palette changes. This allows swapping theme palettes without touching component code.
- Proportional gutters are generated from a single baseSpacing token (baseSpacing = 8px) to keep math simple for engineers, while still allowing density overrides.
- Shadow stacks are simplified to three perceptual presets to reduce cognitive load for engineers and avoid micro-elevation drift. This sacrifices fine-grained elevation variations for consistency.

Artifacts and links:
- Figma board: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/design-surface-gutters-2026 (working frames + token examples)
- PRD: https://docs.redwood.com/confluence/display/DS/Surface+Variants+and+Gutters+PRD
- Branch/Work-in-progress PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-tokens/pull/214 (token definitions + tests)

Rollout plan:
1) Merge token definitions behind feature flag in design system package.
2) Ship changes to non-critical components (internal docs, marketing micro-widgets) to validate build pipeline.
3) Run codemods on buttons and small atom components, followed by a canary release to staging.
4) Expand codemods to tables/charts and monitor visual regressions via Percy + manual spot-checks.
5) Remove old tokens in a follow-up deprecation ticket after 2 cycles.

Testing & QA:
- Visual regression baseline in Percy for each component family.
- Automated contrast checks against WCAG AA for text tokens on each surface.
- Performance: ensure token generation does not increase bundle size by more than 2%.

Migration notes for engineers:
- Use semantic tokens (surface-*) in CSS/JS and avoid referencing palette colors directly.
- For spacing, prefer gutter-* tokens; when necessary, use calc(baseSpacing * factor) to compute spacing in places with dynamic density.

Acceptance criteria: (must pass before Done)
- Token definitions merged and shipped to branch behind flag.
- Two components (Button + Table) migrated with codemods and reviewed by Engineering and QA.
- Accessibility pass (contrast checks and one manual audit) completed.
- Percy baselines created and approved for migrated components.
comments: 2026-03-03 - Alyssa Chen: Initial kickoff meeting with PM and Eng. Agreed on semantic surface approach; engineering prefers a small set of derived tokens to keep runtime cheap.

2026-03-07 - Eng review (Samir Gupta): Raised a concern about legacy theme compatibility; proposed a runtime alias layer so older theme names continue to resolve to new semantic tokens during the migration window.
